mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 1.5%, market expectations for future rate cuts diminish, reducing discount rates and increasing present value of expected corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds or signals hold in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average during the same window, or FEDFUNDS closes below 1.5 for two consecutive months within the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS up and UNRATE down by at least 0.2 percentage points, or the correlation between the two proxies falls below 0.7 in the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, prompting market participants to anticipate higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% while INDPRO decreases over the next month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative despite the defined HOUST/INDPRO pattern, or the cross-correlation between the two proxies turns negative over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in manufacturing output (INDPRO below 99 for two consecutive months) coupled with elevated consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 276) suggests persistent supply-side frictions, which typically precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 99 for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > 276
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained INDPRO weakness and elevated CPIAUCSL, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 273 followed by a sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE above 4.8%) indicates a disinflationary shock that reduces policy rate expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 273 AND UNRATE > 4.8 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive despite the defined CPIAUCSL/UNRATE pattern, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.05 in a 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, unanticipated drop in job openings (PAYEMS) by more than 20,000 in a single month while the unemployment rate remains flat suggests labor market cooling, which reduces growth expectations and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >20,000 in a single month with UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during the cooling episode, or UNRATE declines in response to the PAYEMS drop.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating retail sales growth (HOUST) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift toward consumption-led growth, which elevates equity risk premia and typically produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases at an accelerating rate while INDPRO remains flat or declines over two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) during the consumption acceleration, or the cross-correlation between HOUST and INDPRO turns positive over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 273 for three consecutive months) in the absence of a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests persistent cost pressures that depress earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 273 for three consecutive months AND INDPRO does not fall
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 273 and INDPRO not declining, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
